recommendation: Keep the audit as-is. If dormant `source/us` or commented US Core profile files should be cleaned up, treat that as a separate human-reviewed repository hygiene task rather than a FHIR-12384 spec correction.
issue_request: FHIR-12384 was Published with resolution Persuasive with Modification. It requested moving US-realm/US Core Patient extensions out of FHIR core and, as modified by US Realm, leaving a core page or registry path to realm-specific extension definitions.
initial_application: January 2017 commits for FHIR-12384 repointed old US Core URLs, disabled the dedicated Patient example showing US extensions, and commented out the `us-core` profile entry in `source/fhir.ini`.
additional_context: The old `source/profiles/us-core-*` and `source/us` files still exist, but the active profile entry is commented out. FHIR-39392 later added an active Patient/Provenance example that references the external US Core race extension to demonstrate targeting an extension; this is not a core definition. Current build URLs for the old core US Core extension, value set, and dedicated example pages return 404.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was made because the current built specification is already correct for FHIR-12384.

related_jiras.note: Added the active Patient/Provenance example that references the external US Core race extension; it explains why a US Core URL remains in build-scope examples.
